central_question: Why do lipstick, underwear and hemlines survive as economic stories even when the evidence is thin?

verified_claims.claim: The Lipstick Index is a media-friendly recession hypothesis with contested evidence, not a dependable macro predictor.
The Men’s Underwear Index is popularly attributed to Alan Greenspan but remains weakly evidenced as a formal macro signal.
Skyscraper recession claims are better handled as correlation folklore or contested cycle story than as prediction law.
Hemline evidence is optional folklore and should not carry central argument weight.

myth_or_uncertainty_notes: Do not claim lipstick or underwear sales predict recessions.
visual_opportunities: [VISUAL: myth-versus-measure object row — lipstick, underwear, skyscraper silhouette]
prohibited_or_unsupported_claims: Greenspan formally published the Men’s Underwear Index as a reliable Fed tool.
Lipstick reliably rises in every downturn.
